This module provides an in-depth introduction to the role of energy data in planning, monitoring, and evaluation (PM&E) for sustainable energy development.

It highlights how reliable, up-to-date, and ethically sourced data underpin evidence-based decision-making, policy formulation, and the monitoring of progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG7)—ensuring affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all by 2030.

Participants will explore the importance of standardized frameworks for data reporting, key performance indicators (KPIs), and common PM&E principles, as well as challenges such as data accessibility, quality, and ethical considerations in developing contexts.

Additionally, the module introduces innovative tools, techniques, and trends—such as data science applications, energy modeling, and artificial intelligence—and their relevance for energy systems transformation.

Identify how reliable and ethically sourced data informs evidence-based decision-making, supports sustainable energy policies, and promotes equity and inclusivity in energy access.

Understand the principles behind strategic energy planning, monitoring, and evaluation, and how data and indicators—when analyzed through gender and intersectional perspectives—can strengthen policy and project frameworks.

Examine key data science methods, energy modeling tools, and emerging technologies, assessing their relevance, limitations, and potential to support equitable and innovative energy transitions, particularly in developing contexts.
